findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: The function constructs a SQL query using string interpolation with owner_id directly embedded in the query string. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL code by providing a malicious owner_id value, potentially leading to data exfiltration, unauthorized access, or database manipulation.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker provides owner_id = "'; DROP TABLE orders; --". The query becomes SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '''; DROP TABLE orders; --". The database executes the DROP TABLE command, destroying all order data.
findings.suggestion:
def load_order_rows(owner_id: str, cursor: object) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    """Load queued order rows for one owner through an open cursor."""
    cursor.execute("SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = %s", (owner_id,))
    return [dict(row) for row in cursor.fetchall()]
findings.title: SQL injection vulnerability in load_order_rows
